'''''Someone to Watch Over Me''''' is a 1987 American [[neo-noir film|neo-noir]] [[romantic thriller film]] directed by [[Ridley Scott]] and written by [[Howard Franklin]]. It stars [[Tom Berenger]] as a police detective who has to protect a wealthy woman ([[Mimi Rogers]]), who is a key witness in a murder trial. The film's soundtrack includes the [[George Gershwin|George]] and [[Ira Gershwin|Ira]] Gershwin [[Someone to Watch Over Me (song)|song]] from which the film takes its title, recorded by [[Sting (musician)|Sting]], and [[Vangelis]]' "Memories of Green", originally from Scott's ''[[Blade Runner]]'' (1982).

''Someone to Watch Over Me'' was released by [[Columbia Pictures]] on October 9, 1987. The film received mixed to positive reviews from critics but was a [[box office bomb]], grossing $10.3{{nbsp}}million against a $12.8{{nbsp}}million budget.

==Plot==
Socialite Claire Gregory attends a party and art show sponsored by one of her oldest friends, Winn Hockings. Accompanying her is her straitlaced boyfriend, Neil Steinhart. In another part of town, there is another party, this one for newly appointed [[NYPD]] detective Mike Keegan.

Winn is accosted by a former partner, Joey Venza, who is angry because Winn had not come to him to borrow money for his new art studio. After a short argument, he stabs Winn to death. Claire witnesses the killing, screams, and is spotted by Venza. He pursues her, but she manages to get back into the elevator just in time.

The police are called in, including Keegan. He is a married man, but immediately falls for Claire. Along with fellow cops, he is assigned to protect Claire until Venza is arrested and she can make a positive ID and later testify in court.

Keegan is determined to protect Claire and goes to extremes to do so. Venza makes numerous threats and attempts on her life, nearly succeeding at one point. Keegan and his wife Ellie separate over his involvement with Claire. He and Claire acknowledge their love but Keegan cannot bring himself to simply abandon his family.

At the end, Venza, who draws out Keegan by taking his son hostage, is shot by Ellie and killed. Claire breaks up with Neil and intends to go to Europe to get over Keegan, who returns to his wife and son.

==Production==
The film was initially pitched to Scott in 1982 during a dinner party by [[Howard Franklin]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=https://catalog.afi.com/Film/57821-SOMEONE-TOWATCHOVERME?sid=4f73e1e7-ac66-4ca6-a958-fbece160de30&sr=16.021748&cp=1&pos=0 |title=Someone To Watch Over Me (1987) |publisher=[[American Film Institute]] |access-date=May 21, 2020}}</ref> It was primarily written by Franklin by late 1982 with Scott years later bringing in [[Danilo Bach]] and [[David Seltzer]] to refine it.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite book |title=The Ridley Scott Encyclopedia |first=Lawrence |last=Raw |year=2009 |publisher=[[Scarecrow Press]] |location=[[Plymouth]] |isbn=978-0-8108-6952-3 |page=123 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xBGFacfGR0gC&q=someone+to+watch+over+me+ridley+scott+1982+script%2C+filmed+1986&pg=PA123|access-date=May 21, 2020 |url-access=limited |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> [[Ridley Scott]] made the film following ''[[Legend (1985 film)|Legend]]'' which had been a notable box office failure. In July 1986 [[Alan Ladd, Jr.]] announced the film would be made for [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Movie no Bomb Guide, Filmmaker Says |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |date=1986-07-11 |page=17}}</ref> By September the project had shifted to [[Columbia Pictures]] where [[David Puttnam]], who produced Scott's debut feature ''[[The Duellists]]'', was head of production.<ref>{{cite news |first=Steve |last=Pond |title=David Puttnam's New Deals |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=25 Sep 1986 |page=B7}}</ref> [[Tom Berenger]] was cast in the lead role on the strength of his performance in ''[[Platoon (film)|Platoon]]''.

[[Principal photography]] began on December 8, 1986, with the shoot lasting thirteen weeks. Locations included the [[Bergdorf Goodman Building]], [[Central Park]], [[Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum|Guggenheim Museum]] and various streets on the [[Upper East Side]]. Production moved to [[Burbank Studios]] on January 19, 1987, to film the interior of Miss Gregory's apartment and Mike Keegan's home in Queens. The interiors used for the [[nightclub]] scenes were filmed on the {{RMS|Queen Mary}} docked in [[Long Beach, California|Long Beach]].<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite book |first=Vincent |last=LoBrutto  |title=Ridley Scott: A Biography |date=17 May 2019 |page=100 |publisher=[[University Press of Kentucky]] |location=[[Lexington, Kentucky|Lexington]] |isbn=978-0-8131-7711-3 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=WGmNDwAAQBAJ&q=someone+to+watch+over+me+ridley+scott+1982+script%2C+filmed+1986&pg=PT100 |access-date=May 21, 2020 |url-access=limited |via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref>

==Release==
''Someone to Watch Over Me'' was released in the United States on October 9, 1987. It was the first film greenlit by Puttnam to be released, but by the time it was released, Puttnam had resigned.<ref>Lost tycoon. Malcolm, Derek; Goodwin, Chris. The Guardian (1959-2003); London (UK) 19 Sep 1987: 19.</ref>

===Home media===
The film was originally released in the United States on [[VHS]] in May 1988 and did better on home video.<ref>{{cite news|title=VIDEO CHARTS : Babies Booming, 'East L.A.' Rising|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-05-26-ca-4899-story.html|access-date=July 4, 2012}}</ref> It was first released on remastered DVD in October 1999 by [[Sony Pictures]] with [[widescreen]] and full-screen format options, including production notes and theatrical trailers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blu-ray.com/dvd/Someone-to-Watch-Over-Me-DVD/8943/|title=Someone to Watch Over Me DVD|website=Blu-ray.com|accessdate=January 11, 2020}}</ref> [[Shout! Factory]] released it on [[Blu-ray]] under their Shout Select banner on March 12, 2019, including two new extra features, an interview with screenwriter [[Howard Franklin]] and an interview with director of photography [[Steven Poster]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Someone-to-Watch-Over-Me-Blu-ray/226048/|title=Someone to Watch Over Me Blu-ray|website=Blu-ray.com|date=March 12, 2019|accessdate=January 11, 2020}}</ref> Powerhouse Films (Indicator) released the film in the U.K. on limited edition Blu-ray on May 17, 2021, in a 2k restoration containing the aforementioned extras from Shout as well as a new audio commentary from filmmaker and film historian [[Jim Hemphill]] and the theatrical trailer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blu-ray.com/movies/Someone-to-Watch-Over-Me-Blu-ray/266891/|title=Someone to Watch Over Me Blu-ray United Kingdom|website=Blu-ray.com|date=17 May 2021|accessdate=9 June 2021}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Box office===
In the United States and Canada, ''Someone to Watch Over Me'' grossed $10.3{{nbsp}}million at the box office,<ref name=BOM>{{Cite Box Office Mojo |access-date=2025-01-13}}</ref> against a budget of $12.8{{nbsp}}million<ref>{{Cite news |first=David T. |last=Friendly |title=David Picker: Out of the Cold, Into Columbia |date=1986-12-04 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |page=1}}</ref> It opened at No.{{nbsp}}4, its first of four consecutive weeks in the Top{{nbsp}}10 at the domestic box office.<ref name=BOM/>

===Critical response===
{{RT data|prose|consensus=Its plot is sometimes hard to swallow, but some fine acting and director Ridley Scott's stylish visual flair make ''Someone to Watch Over Me'' an engaging police thriller.|ref=yes}} [[Metacritic]], which uses a [[Weighted arithmetic mean|weighted average]], assigned the film a score of 55 out of 100, based on 15 critics, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.<ref name="Metacritic">{{cite web |title=''Someone to Watch Over Me'' |url=https://www.metacritic.com/movie/someone-to-watch-over-me |website=[[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[Fandom (website)#Fandom, Inc.|Fandom, Inc.]] |access-date=2025-01-13 |archive-url= |archive-date= |url-status=}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B+" on an A+ to F scale.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cinemascore |url=https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181220122629/https://www.cinemascore.com/publicsearch/index/title/ |archive-date=2018-12-20}}</ref>

[[Roger Ebert]] gave the film two stars out of four and wrote: {{Blockquote
|text=There is something fundamentally wrong with a script in which the hero sleeps with the wrong woman. I am not talking here in moral terms, but in story terms. The makers of this film got so carried away by their High Concept that they missed the point of the whole story.<ref name=Ebert>{{cite news |first=Roger |last=Ebert |author-link=Roger Ebert |title=Someone to Watch Over Me movie review |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=1987-10-09 |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/someone-to-watch-over-me-1987 |access-date=2025-01-13 |via=[[RogerEbert.com]]}}</ref>}} He did, however, praise Lorraine Bracco for playing her role "with great force and imagination."<ref name=Ebert/> [[Vincent Canby]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote: {{Blockquote|text=Nothing that happens to these three characters is moving or even exciting. To keep the movie going until its absurd ending, the character of the murderer is changed, midstream, from an ordinary, run-of-the-mill New York mobster into a crazed psychotic. Howard Franklin's screenplay plays less like a feature film than like the pilot for a failed television series about New York policemen.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Vincent |last=Canby |author-link=Vincent Canby |title=Film: 'Someone to Watch Over Me' |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=1987-10-09 |page=C40 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/10/09/movies/film-someone-to-watch-over-me.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=2025-01-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230413193045/https://www.nytimes.com/1987/10/09/movies/film-someone-to-watch-over-me.html |archive-date=2023-04-13 |url-status=live}}</ref>}} ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' called the film "a stylish and romantic police thriller which manages, through the sleek direction of Ridley Scott and persuasive ensemble performances, to triumph over several hard-to-swallow plot developments."<ref>{{Cite magazine |author=<!--not stated, generic "Staff"--> |title=Someone To Watch Over Me |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |department=Film |date=1987-08-30 |url=https://variety.com/1986/film/reviews/someone-to-watch-over-me-1200427113/ |access-date=2025-01-13}}</ref> John Ferguson of ''[[Radio Times]]'' awarded it four stars out of five, describing it as an "intelligent thriller" which "remains one of Ridley Scott's most quietly satisfying works". He wrote that "it may lack the power of the director's ''[[Gladiator (2000 film)|Gladiator]]'', ''[[Thelma & Louise]]'' and ''[[Blade Runner]]'', but this is still beautifully shot and remains a stylish affair", and he praised the performances as "first rate".<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Someone to Watch Over Me |first=John |last=Ferguson |magazine=[[Radio Times]] |year=1987 |url=https://www.radiotimes.com/movie-guide/b-tbcs60/someone-to-watch-over-me/ |access-date=2021-12-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205063651/https://www.radiotimes.com/movie-guide/b-tbcs60/someone-to-watch-over-me/ |archive-date=2021-12-05 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Michael Wilmington of the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' called the film "an erotic culture-clash thriller that's almost swoony with glamour and romance. The movie is exciting, richly textured. But, despite its high quality, there's something unformed about it, like a poem that doesn't quite sing, a painting with a color missing."<ref>{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Wilmington |title=Looks at Love's Dark, Light Sides |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=1987-10-09 |page=VI-1}}</ref> Rita Kempley of ''[[The Washington Post]]'' called it "a reasonably enjoyable romantic thriller" that "shows off director Ridley Scott's extraordinary visual artistry. The sets are so sumptuous, you'll want to move right in. But the haze is so thick, you'll need to bring a defogger. Scott, who directed ''[[Alien (film)|Alien]]'' and ''Blade Runner'', looks at the world through veils of smog. What with these pictorial pollutants, he loses sight of plot."<ref>{{cite news |first=Rita |last=Kempley |title=Kiss and Yell |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=1987-10-09 |page=B7 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1987/10/09/kiss-and-yell/d69c3889-3979-49b5-972a-118ead1ab190/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=2025-01-13}}</ref> [[Pauline Kael]] observed in ''[[The New Yorker]]'' that Scott "has put so much morbid, finicky care into this silly little story that he's worried the fun out of it."<ref>{{cite magazine |first=Pauline |last=Kael |author-link=Pauline Kael |title=The Current Cinema |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=1987-11-02 |page=140}}</ref>
